note: Reachability was checked when this list was built. Sources marked enabled:false are documented rather than deleted, so the reason stays visible and can be retried — several of them block datacentre IPs and may work fine from a laptop.

sources.name: Publishers Weekly
sources.note: The trade record of what is actually being published. Every review page prints publisher, page count and ISBN - the two dimensions (scale, provenance) the catalogue leaves dark for a book published this year. Reviews are short, so PW rarely carries a book on its own; its value is that it merges with the longer reviews elsewhere and supplies their missing metadata. Named in §8 of the profile as acceptable critical evidence.

sources.name: Book Marks (Lit Hub)
sources.note: Lit Hub's review aggregator. Its weekly Best Reviewed list is a dozen books per post, each line carrying title, author, publisher and a tally of how the critics landed - the nearest thing to a consensus signal in any of these sources. Goodreads retired its feeds and StoryGraph, LibraryThing and Bookshop all refuse automated clients, so this plus Open Library ratings is the reader- and aggregate-opinion coverage available.

sources.name: The New York Review of Books
sources.note: The main /feed/ is empty; the ?post_type=article variant carries the reviews. Article pages expose a Reviewed: block with publisher and page count.

sources.name: London Review of Books
sources.note: Feed titles are 'Critic: Headline' and carry no book. The article page has a reviewed-items block with title, author, translator, publisher, pages and date, and an icon-book / icon-film class that says whether a book is under review at all.

sources.name: Los Angeles Review of Books
sources.note: No RSS since the Next.js rebuild. Listing and article bodies both come out of the embedded __NEXT_DATA__ payload.

sources.name: The New Yorker
sources.note: The books-only feeds 404 and 400; the everything feed carries them and is filtered on path.

sources.name: The Guardian — Fiction
sources.note: Titles follow 'Title by Author review - standfirst', which parses without touching the article page.

sources.name: The New York Times Book Review
sources.note: Headlines are "Book Review: ‘Title,’" so the section prefix and the wrapping quotes come off before anything else looks at the title.

sources.name: The Atlantic — Books
sources.note: Full review text ships in the feed, entity-encoded, with the book title in <em> and the author as a possessive in front of it.

sources.name: Harper's Magazine
sources.disabledReason: The public feed is Weekly Review, events and announcements; the criticism sits behind the archive with no reliable marker to isolate it.

sources.name: The New Republic

sources.name: Los Angeles Times — Books
sources.note: The books channel carries a lot of arts news; anything that is not a review simply fails to resolve to a book and stays out of the feed.

sources.name: Full Stop
sources.note: Reviews live under /reviews/ and title as "Book - Author", which parses without an article fetch. Small-press heavy, which is where D7 pays.

sources.name: Literary Hub
sources.note: High volume and mostly not reviews, so it is filtered hard on the title.
sources.disabledReason: The main feed is essays, excerpts and the daily round-up rather than reviews. Book Marks is the review arm and has no feed.

sources.name: Kirkus Reviews
sources.note: Headline is the book title in caps; the author is a slug in the review URL. Covers every genre, so the fiction filter does more work here than elsewhere.

sources.name: The Times Literary Supplement
sources.disabledReason: 403 to datacentre IPs. Worth retrying from a laptop. Checked 2026-08-24: the whole domain is gated, not just the feed path, so scraping does not help from a blocked network either.

sources.name: Bookforum
sources.note: RSS has been dead since the relaunch. The site is Nuxt and ships its page state as window.__NUXT__, which carries a publications array - title, author, publisher, ISBN, page count - plus the full review body. Tier-1 data, better than the feed ever gave.

sources.name: n+1
sources.disabledReason: Reachable now that the user-agent is honest, and still not a review feed: the magazine files essays, fiction and politics. Measured 2026-08-28: 60 items, 0 books.

sources.name: Public Books
sources.note: Academic and ideas nonfiction, reviewed at length by the people who teach it. Recorded as CAPTCHA-blocked from 2026-08-24 and reachable from 2026-08-29: the block was the Chrome user-agent, not the address. It answered an honest one on the first try.

sources.name: The Baffler
sources.disabledReason: 403 to datacentre IPs. Checked 2026-08-24: the whole domain is gated, not just the feed path, so scraping does not help from a blocked network either.

sources.name: 4Columns

sources.name: LSE Review of Books
sources.note: Academic nonfiction reviewed at length: economics, politics, history, sociology. The closest thing to a Kirkus for university-press books, and the strongest single addition for a nonfiction reader.

sources.name: The Georgia Review
sources.note: Feed titles are literally "on TITLE by AUTHOR", which is a house format as clean as the Guardian's. Worth a titlePattern parser rather than the prose fallback.

sources.name: The Kenyon Review
sources.note: Long-form reviews and criticism alongside the fiction. Mixed feed, so extraction has to carry it.

sources.name: The Common
sources.note: Amherst-based. Reviews, translation and place-writing.
sources.disabledReason: Fiction, poetry and place-writing. Reviews sit elsewhere on the site. Measured 2026-08-28: 8 items, 0 books.

sources.name: The Point
sources.note: Essays on books and ideas. Long, argued, usually about a specific title.
sources.disabledReason: Essays about ideas, occasionally departing from a book. No book under review in the feed. Measured 2026-08-28: 10 items, 0 books.

sources.name: Guernica
sources.note: Politics and literature. Reviews are a minority of the feed but they are substantial when they come.

sources.name: World Literature Today
sources.note: Translation and world literature, and the only source here that covers books published outside English-language trade routinely.

sources.name: Words Without Borders
sources.note: Translation. The monthly Watchlist is a roundup of several books at once, which the aggregator handles the way it handles Book Marks.

sources.name: NPR Books
sources.note: General-audience reviews, fiction and nonfiction in roughly equal measure. Wide, mainstream, and the register a wider audience actually reads.

sources.name: Christian Science Monitor Books
sources.note: Steady general-audience reviewing, heavier on nonfiction and history than most.
sources.disabledReason: Reviews are real but the book is named only in quotation marks inside the standfirst, and the headline is a magazine headline. Nothing to extract from without an article parser. Measured 2026-08-28: 20 items, 0 books.

sources.name: The Economist — Culture
sources.note: Nonfiction-forward, short, and covers economics, history and politics titles nothing else here touches. The feed carries the whole culture desk, so section filtering matters.
sources.disabledReason: The feed is the whole culture desk: film, television, music and obituaries, with book pieces a small minority and no book named in a parseable way. Sixty items an hour for nothing. Measured 2026-08-28: 60 items, 0 books.

sources.name: The American Scholar

sources.name: Dissent

sources.name: The Critic

sources.name: New Books Network
sources.note: Author interviews across a hundred channels, covering exactly the university presses that publish press releases rather than catalogues. Every episode is filed as Author, "Title" (Publisher, Year), which is more structure than any review feed here offers. It is an interview rather than a review, so it is marked critical: false and supplies existence and metadata without ever moving a score.
